# Phase 6 — the real-time architecture

*Generated by `hydrocascade realtime` on 2026-09-24.*

## The honest scope statement — Doc 09 §1.1

> **What we deliver:** a validated model, a fully specified deployment architecture, and a working replay-mode dashboard that reproduces the Wayanad event as if live.
>
> **What we do not deliver:** a running, monitored, 24/7 production service.

Doc 09 §1.1 is blunt about why this is said plainly: *"A semester project that claims a live operational system and cannot show one loses more credibility than it gains."*

## The latency budget — the constraint that shapes everything

| Stage | Latency |
|---|---|
| Rain falls | T + 0 |
| **GPM IMERG Early Run available** | **T + 4 h** |
| Ingest, regrid, update accumulations | + 10 min |
| Recompute intensity across all units | + 2 min |
| Alert evaluation and dashboard refresh | + 1 min |
| **Total: rain to updated risk** | **≈ 4 h 15 min** |

**Therefore this is a nowcast layer with roughly four hours of latency. It is not a siren.** Wayanad failed at 02:17 IST; rainfall from 22:00 the previous night would have been reflected in the system by about 02:00. The value is in the *hours to days* of rising signal beforehand, not in the final minutes. This is the first thing an operational agency asks, so it is stated before anything else.

## The ERA5-Land problem, and the fix — Doc 09 §1.3

ERA5-Land soil moisture is the physically correct wetness variable and has multi-day latency, so it **cannot be used in real time**. The fix is an antecedent precipitation index built from rainfall alone (`API_t = k · API_{t-1} + P_t`, k = 0.9), calibrated offline against ERA5-Land and used at run time. ERA5-Land is used for fitting only. The API is currently the top-ranked flood driver in `reports/phase3_drivers.md`, which is at least consistent with it carrying the wetness signal it is meant to.

## The processing loop — Doc 09 §1.4

```
HOURLY    fetch IMERG Early -> regrid -> update R1..R30 and API
          -> recompute mu_i -> decay active excitation, drop expired
          -> recompute lambda_i, P_i, bands -> alerts -> snapshot
DAILY     fetch GloFAS -> Q2 exceedance + declustering -> append
          confirmed floods to the live history
ON EVENT  validate and append with its mark -> look up the affected
          set (landslide: Down(pi(x)) within max travel time;
          flood: downstream reaches + the slope corridor)
          -> recompute lambda ONLY for those units   [incremental]
          -> re-evaluate alerts; push if a level rises
          target: under 2 seconds
```

The incremental path is what makes NFR-03 achievable: temporal truncation leaves only a few hundred active events, and network truncation limits each to a few hundred reaches, so the update is a handful of vectorised operations rather than a refit.

**Measured here:** one full likelihood evaluation over the training catalog takes about 0.4 s on this laptop, against the NFR-01 budget of 60 s. The margin is the reason the hourly recompute is not a concern.

## Failure handling — Doc 09 §1.6

| Failure | Response |
|---|---|
| IMERG feed unavailable | persist last known accumulations, flag the dashboard **STALE** with its age, never silently extrapolate |
| GloFAS unavailable | skip flood detection for the day, log it |
| A unit produces `nan` | mark **UNKNOWN**, never Normal; log and alert the operator |
| Model state corrupted | rebuild from the event history, which is the single source of truth |

> **Rule: the system never shows "Normal" when it means "I don't know."**
